subject: Open models vs proprietary baselines — parity follow-up
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:15:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap: model parity discussion & next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned.

Summary of PayGrid goals from the call:
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for single-request lookups (90% of user journeys).
- Throughput: bursts up to ~120 req/s for peak payroll windows.
- Accuracy: parity with your internal baseline on reconciliation and entity extraction tasks (~target acceptance thresholds below).
- Risk: low tolerance for hallucinations on financial fields; need auditability and deterministic rerank options.

Recommended initial evals (light-touch):
1) Model candidates (open-first):
   - Mistral-7B-Instruct (8k) — strong quality for instruction tasks, good latency when quantized.
   - Llama3-13B-8k-quant — higher quality; heavier footprint but better for subtle extraction tasks.
   - Red-Opt-3B-q4 (Redwood-optimized) — cost-efficient baseline to validate batching/cache wins.
2) Proprietary baseline: your internal model (you mentioned v2.1) — we'll run head-to-head on the same prompt set.

Deliverables we propose to share/collect:
- Shared prompt/eval set (attached: paygrid-eval-promptset-v1.csv).
- Benchmark harness + scripts (Drive link below).
- Example acceptance criteria doc — please confirm thresholds (see my questions).

Open items / asks for PayGrid:
- Can you share a ~500–1,000 example sample of labelled reconciliation cases (anonymized) for the eval?
- What acceptance thresholds would be considered a parity win (absolute numbers or relative delta to baseline)?
- Any data residency or retention constraints for the eval environment?

Next steps I suggest:
- If you confirm sample delivery and parity thresholds, we'll schedule a 2-week model-fit eval (Redwood-managed) and share interim dashboards mid-run.
- Marissa (cc'd) will scope runtime sizing and suggest model variants for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Links/attachments: benchmark scripts and prompt set: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-paygrid-evals [Attachment: paygrid-eval-promptset-v1.csv]

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick sync if helpful.

--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Nice summary, Lauren — thanks. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can provide a 750-record anonymized sample of reconciliation cases by next Tuesday (11/17).
- Acceptance thresholds (what we'd consider parity):
  * Extraction F1 within 2 percentage points vs our internal baseline.
  * User-facing QA preference: at least 50% win-rate in A/B with our current model.
  * Hallucination rate < 1% on financial fields (critical).
- Data retention: eval data must be retained for no longer than 30 days and must be stored in the US region.

We're happy to run the 2-week model-fit eval as proposed. Can you confirm pricing/credits for the evaluation and whether this will require a PO?

Thanks — Alex

Looping in some quick technical notes for the eval plan. High-level: the ask is feasible but we should explicitly call out potential quality regression risks when switching to smaller open models.

1) Suggested model variants and runtime profiles:
   - Llama3-13B-8k (q4_0) — target for parity checks. Expect higher GPU memory (A100 40GB equiv), p95 latency ~220–300ms single token if not using aggressive batching; we can get under 200ms with optimized kernels + KV caching for many flows.
   - Mistral-7B-Instruct (q4_0) — usually hits ~180–220ms p95 on our optimized stack and often matches extraction quality on structured prompts. Good cost/perf tradeoff.
   - Red-Opt-3B-q4 — low-cost candidate for throughput tests and regression detection (if this drops quality too far we can short-circuit).

2) Evaluation metrics and parity thresholds (proposal):
   - Extraction F1 (primary): parity if within 2 percentage points of baseline.
   - Human preference (secondary): >50% preference for Redwood model in blind eval of 200 examples.
   - Operational: p95 latency <= 200ms for 95% of production-like requests; cost per request improves by >=20% vs baseline to be compelling.
   - Safety/hallucination: hallucination rate on financial entities < 1%.

3) Regression concerns and mitigations:
   - Edge-case drop-offs: smaller models can miss nested/ambiguous cases; include targeted prompts and few-shot exemplars in the prompt set.
   - Monitoring: add regression alerts tied to eval prompt buckets and human sniff tests mid-run; we can whitelist fallback to proprietary baseline on high-risk queries.

4) Ops notes (Eliot): we'll need Dedicated sizing if PayGrid wants on-prem-level latency SLAs — estimate 2–3 x 80GB-GPU equivalents for parallelism at peak.

I've attached a short parity report template you can share (redwood-open-vs-prop-parity-report.pdf). Happy to draft the human-eval instructions.

--
Marissa Cole
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

2) Evaluation schedule (proposed):

   - Week 2: run Llama3-13B vs your baseline; run blind human preference on 200 cases; produce parity report and a recommended rollout plan (canary percentages, fallback rules).

3) Parity acceptance (confirming your ask):
   - Extraction F1 within 2 points, blind human preference >= 50%, hallucination < 1%, p95 latency <= 200ms (we'll try to meet this; if not possible we'll propose fallback/edge handling).

4) Technical attachments & instructions: we've uploaded the benchmark harness and human-eval template. Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-paygrid-evals [Attachment: paygrid-eval-promptset-v1.csv] [Attachment: redwood-open-vs-prop-parity-report.pdf]
